title: Terry Thompson
summary: President & Co-Founder. A lifelong commitment to turning possibility into practical support.
label: People / Founder

sections.title: A purpose shaped by experience
paragraphs: Terry Thompson co-founded America On Track with Claire Braeburn in 1995. As President and Project Director of several programs, she combines leadership, program development and hands-on work with schools, families, mentors and community partners.

sections.title: From literature to community leadership
paragraphs: Terry began working at age 11 and graduated from high school at 15. French was her first language; reading Victor Hugo’s Les Misérables at 14 shaped her interest in compassion and social justice.

At 17, she came to the United States on her own. She worked her way through college, initially studying music composition before earning a BA in literature, magna cum laude, from California State University, Long Beach. Her published biography also describes a two-year MFA program and a Certified Financial Planner designation from USC, followed by her own financial planning business.

sections.title: Building America On Track
paragraphs: After researching the challenges facing Orange County communities, Terry and Claire brought their experience and resources together to establish an independent nonprofit. Their work developed into youth leadership, mentoring, health education and prevention programs.

Terry’s approach emphasizes teamwork, diversity, innovation and collaboration. She believes an organization must be able to turn its purpose into action, and stays connected to that work through direct relationships with participants, volunteers and partners.

sections.title: Beyond the programs
paragraphs: Terry enjoys reading, gardening and concerts with her family. Her biography describes gardening as a form of meditation and an interest in plant-based nutrition. She lives in Orange County with her husband, near their two daughters and their families.

sections.title: Recognition
paragraphs: Terry and Claire received the President’s Service Award at the White House in November 1998, according to the organization’s awards archive. Their work has also received local and state recognition.

title: Claire Braeburn
summary: Executive Director & Co-Founder. Connecting public service, practical leadership and community action.
label: People / Founder

sections.title: Putting ideas into action
paragraphs: Claire Braeburn co-founded America On Track with Terry Thompson in 1995. Her background in computer technology, marketing and public speaking helped establish both the organization and the infrastructure supporting its programs.

sections.title: An early commitment to service
paragraphs: At UCLA, Claire worked as a Community Service Officer for the university’s Police Department and volunteered with the UCLA Medical Center, Children’s Ward and Prison Coalition. Work at a publishing company producing motivational books and recordings reinforced her interest in positive action.

She served as president of her Toastmasters International club and received public-speaking awards. After graduating from UCLA, she developed a career in public speaking and community leadership, trained in Neuro Associative Conditioning with Anthony Robbins, and conducted business and training seminars throughout Southern California.

sections.title: Founding and strengthening the organization
paragraphs: Following a year of research with Terry, Claire helped launch America On Track. Their programs grew through partnerships, practical improvements and a sustained focus on youth. In June 2000, Claire earned a Certification in Financial Planning and Management for Nonprofit Organizations from California State University, Fullerton.

sections.title: Coalitions and public service
paragraphs: In 1997, Attorney General Dan Lungren appointed Claire to a 14-month term on the statewide Youth Council on Violence Prevention. She was the only adult representative from Orange County.

Her published biography records service as a founding member of the Violence Prevention Coalition of Orange County, participant in the Irvine Prevention Coalition, Treasurer of the Orange County Mentoring Partnership, and Chair of the Santa Ana Weed & Seed SPIRIT & SAINT Coalitions.

Claire has participated in the Tobacco and Vape Free OC Coalition since 1997. Elected Chairperson in June 2011, she served two consecutive terms. These are biographical service records; they do not imply that every position is held today.

sections.title: Life beyond work
paragraphs: Claire enjoys running, skiing, kayaking, hiking, concerts and museums. She became vegetarian in 1991 and vegan in 2004. Her biography describes time with her husband and two children, including fostering shelter animals, and her desire to be a positive role model for young people.

title: Recognition, earned over time.
summary: An archive of awards, community recognition and competitive grants from the organization’s first 25 years.
label: Archive / Recognition

sections.title: A record of service
paragraphs: America On Track’s 2020 archive records 21 awards and commendations across its first 25 years, alongside government, corporate and foundation grant support. The entries below preserve that historical record; they are not a claim of new awards or active funding today.

sections.title: National recognition / 1998
paragraphs: In November 1998, Terry Thompson and Claire Braeburn received the President’s Service Award at the White House for outstanding service to youth. The awards archive reports more than 3,500 nominations and 18 national winners.
One Emerging Leaders page gives 1999 for this recognition. This archive follows the November 1998 date recorded on the dedicated awards page.

sections.title: Community and education honors
items: 1996–1997 · Huntington Beach Administrators’ Association Community Service Award for school–community partnerships and work with Westminster High School teens.
1997 · Outstanding Contributions to Education Award, Orange County Department of Education.
1997 · O.C. Spirit of Volunteerism Award, Volunteer Center Orange County and JCPenney.

1997 · Claire Braeburn and teen partner Yen Duong selected to represent Orange County on the Attorney General’s Youth Council on Violence Prevention. The archive reports the highest rating for their completed 14-month project.
June 1998 · A Grass Roots Garden and plaque dedicated to America On Track at Westminster Public Library.
1998 and 2002 · Teen Emerging Leaders received Ambassador of Peace Awards.
1999 · Service to Mankind Award, Sertoma Club of Anaheim.
2000 · Ambassadors of Peace Award, Orange County Violence Prevention Coalition, awarded to Terry Thompson and Claire Braeburn.
2001 · Outstanding Supporters of Prevention Award, Irvine Community Drug Prevention.
2001 · Julie Mayer Award, Anaheim Arts Council, for the Cesar Chavez community mural at Magnolia High School.
2008 · An America On Track-nominated teen mentor received the Disneyland Resort Scholarship.
2009 · Women Making a Difference Award: State Senator Lou Correa recognized the founders’ service to Orange County.
2010 · Santa Ana Community Building Award, Sports & Fitness Initiative of the Year, for helping design Memorial Exercise Park and funding sports equipment.
May 2016 · Tobacco Control Evaluation Center Certificate of Excellence for the final evaluation report on the 2010–2015 California Tobacco Control Program grant.

sections.title: Investments in long-term work
items: 2007, 2011 and 2016 · Multi-year federal Physical Education Program grants. The archive describes America On Track as the only nonprofit organization awarded a competitive three-year PEP grant in the United States in 2016.
2013–2020 · Multi-year Nutrition Education and Obesity Prevention grants from the Orange County Health Care Agency’s Nutrition Services division for SNAP-Ed eligible individuals.
2017 · Sixth consecutive three-year Tobacco Prevention Project grant from the Orange County Health Care Agency.
2020 · Third consecutive five-year On Track for a Tobacco-Free Orange County grant from the California Department of Public Health, California Tobacco Control Program.

sections.title: Recognizing young leaders
paragraphs: The archive also celebrates the organization’s Spirit of Volunteerism Eagle Award for outstanding teen mentors and youth champions who dedicated four or more years to America On Track. It describes college scholarships for qualified Emerging Leaders and mentors; contact the team for current opportunities and eligibility.

sections.title: A quarter-century milestone
paragraphs: In 2020, America On Track marked 25 years of service and thanked its staff, board, partners, funders and participants. That anniversary closes the period covered by this awards archive.

title: The record behind the work.
summary: Published evaluations, historical outcomes and participant experiences, with their context intact.
label: Evidence / Results archive

sections.title: 2019 activity and participation
paragraphs: During 2019, America On Track reported 5,597 classes, presentations, resource booths, health fairs, leadership sessions, merchant trainings and special events across its five core programs at that time.
Those activities generated 259,452 youth and adult service contacts. This total includes people participating repeatedly; it is not a count of unique individuals.

sections.title: How the organization evaluates its work
paragraphs: America On Track describes a long-standing commitment to evidence-based practice and formative evaluation: using findings to improve program decisions. Its published record states that it has worked with the Center for Applied Research Solutions since 1998.

The original results page also describes measures of daily physical activity among 4,552 students in 10 schools, leadership skills, college-going, mentee retention and scholarships. It does not supply clear reporting periods and methods for every measure. We do not present these as current-year performance figures.

sections.title: Additional outcomes in the published archive
paragraphs: The original results page reports the following measures. Its animated counters have been preserved here as readable text. Except where specified, the page does not identify the measurement period, sample size or methodology, so these remain historical reported outcomes rather than current or independently verified rates.
items: 187% increase in the proportion of students engaging in 60 minutes of daily physical activity, in a group of 4,552 students across 10 schools. This is a relative increase, not 187 percentage points.
91% of teen Emerging Leaders improved their leadership skills.
100% of graduating seniors in the Emerging Leaders for Civic Engagement program went on to college.
93% of Brighter Futures mentees planned to attend college or trade school.
96% of Brighter Futures mentees remained active in the program for more than 12 months.
$163,700 in college scholarships awarded since 2009, as reported in the archive; an end date is not specified.

sections.title: Community outcomes in the results archive
paragraphs: The results page records the following historical outcomes. Its housing and trade-school totals describe an earlier snapshot than the separate tobacco-policy record; the two sets should not be added together.
items: 22 new health policies implemented at sites throughout Santa Ana and Buena Park.
Smoke-free parks ordinances passed in Santa Ana in February 2012 and Stanton in July 2018.
79 multi-unit housing complexes, representing 5,294 homes, adopted voluntary 100% smoke-free policies covering units and balconies.
Two trade schools adopted 100% smoke-free campus policies.

80% of participating tobacco retailers achieved 5 Star Merchant status, described in the archive as not selling alcohol or tobacco illegally to youth. The page does not state a reporting period or sample size for this percentage.

sections.title: College begins to feel possible
paragraphs: A College Is for Me Too! summer camp participant described the experience as evidence that someone cared and that college was an option. A former Brighter Futures mentee, later in college and working, described returning as a mentor to offer others the support they had received.

sections.title: Angel’s experience
paragraphs: In an account published when he was 12 and starting seventh grade, Angel Lopez described how Brighter Futures supported him after years of housing instability and parental incarceration. He reported earning A’s and B’s and described the program as helping children discover possibilities they had not imagined.
This is a historical participant account, not a statement about Angel’s circumstances today.

sections.title: Sy and Joseph / a sustained connection
paragraphs: America On Track matched 13-year-old Joseph with adult mentor Sy in 2008. Sy supported Joseph through academic, health and social challenges. Five years later, Sy reported that Joseph was employed in warehousing at Disneyland and earning enough to support himself. The archive includes a positive follow-up from Sy in 2020.
Another adult mentor, nearly three years into Brighter Futures, described the relationship as feeling like an extended family connection.

sections.title: Families and schools
paragraphs: The archive includes a parent’s thanks for support in raising her daughters. A K–8 Catholic school principal described three years of fitness and nutrition collaboration, praising the staff’s contribution to students and the wider school community.
These accounts preserve individual perspectives. They are not guarantees of the same outcome for every participant.

sections.title: Need more recent reporting?
paragraphs: Ask America On Track for current evaluations, service totals, methodology or outcomes for a particular program. The historical records here remain dated rather than being relabeled as current results.

title: Prevention has many parts.
summary: Education, youth leadership and healthier environments work together to address tobacco and vape use.
label: Community health / Prevention

sections.title: Work that began in 1997
paragraphs: America On Track has carried out tobacco-use prevention work in Orange County since 1997. The organization combines direct education and community engagement with policy and systems work, including efforts addressing vaping.

sections.title: Two connected projects
paragraphs: One project focuses on lowering young people’s access to tobacco. The other, On Track for a Tobacco-Free Orange County, works to reduce exposure to secondhand smoke. Together they connect individual learning, merchant outreach and changes in community settings.

sections.title: Why the community approach matters
paragraphs: America On Track’s published approach recognizes that product marketing, availability, social norms and unequal access to prevention services affect communities differently. It works with residents and local partners to reach underserved groups and support lasting changes in the places people live, learn and gather.

sections.title: From awareness to action
items: Youth education and high-school leadership clubs.
Parent town halls with schools and law enforcement.
Merchant education and recognition.
Youth and adult workgroups, community events and educational materials.
Resident surveys, policymaker meetings and follow-up technical support.

sections.title: About the public-health context
paragraphs: The earlier website included tobacco cost and prevalence statistics from different periods. Those figures are not presented here as current estimates. These pages describe America On Track’s educational services and historical program record; contact the team for current materials.

title: Make prevention a community effort.
summary: Helping youth, parents, schools and local businesses reduce young people’s access to tobacco and vaping products.
label: Community health / Youth access

sections.title: Start before use becomes a habit
paragraphs: America On Track’s youth-access project brings prevention education together with local action. Its focus is on helping young people understand social pressures and product marketing while engaging the adults and businesses around them.

sections.title: Six practical activities
items: Vaping prevention education for youth.
Parent town hall meetings in partnership with law enforcement and school administrators.
Youth tobacco-control leadership clubs at high schools.
Merchant education.
A social sources campaign addressing access through other people.
The 5 Star Merchant recognition program.

sections.title: Young people have a role
paragraphs: School-based leadership clubs give young people opportunities to participate in tobacco-control work. Parent town halls connect families with educators and law enforcement, while merchant education extends prevention beyond the classroom.

sections.title: A historical data point
paragraphs: The original project page cites 2019 data indicating that one in four high-school students had used e-cigarettes in the previous month. That figure describes the period referenced on the source page; it is not a current Orange County prevalence estimate.

sections.title: Bring the work to your community
paragraphs: Schools, parents, merchants and community groups can contact America On Track to discuss prevention education or partnership opportunities. The team confirms current availability and the appropriate next step.

title: Healthier places to live and gather.
summary: On Track for a Tobacco-Free Orange County connects resident voices with policy and environmental change.
label: Community health / Policy record

sections.title: Reducing exposure to secondhand smoke
paragraphs: Since 2010, America On Track has implemented California Tobacco Control Projects focused on legislative and voluntary policies in Orange County. The work addresses social determinants of health and disparities, with particular attention to communities with high Latino populations and residents facing low incomes or limited educational opportunities.

sections.title: Residents help shape the work
paragraphs: Youth and adult secondhand-smoke workgroups, community events, educational presentations, public-opinion surveys and key-informant interviews help connect local experiences with policy discussions.
America On Track develops educational materials, collaborates with local and state tobacco-control organizations, meets with policymakers, and provides follow-up assistance and technical support.

sections.title: Dated policy milestones
paragraphs: The organization reports supporting the following measures. These are historical program achievements, not a statement of current legal requirements.
items: February 2012 · Santa Ana smoke-free parks ordinance.
July 2018 · Stanton smoke-free parks ordinance.
July 2021 · Buena Park tobacco retail licensing and flavors-ban ordinance.
March 2022 · Santa Ana flavors-ban ordinance.
July 2023 · Buena Park smoke-free city and smoke-free multi-unit housing ordinance.

sections.title: Voluntary policy adoption
paragraphs: The dedicated policy page reports the following cumulative figures without a single reporting date. These supersede the smaller snapshot on the general results page; they are not additional totals to be combined with it.
items: 95 multi-unit housing complexes, representing 6,018 residential units, adopted voluntary 100% smoke-free policies, including individual units and balconies.
39 licensed residential child-care facilities adopted 100% smoke-free policies for their properties.
39 restaurants adopted smoke-free outdoor dining policies.
Five trade schools adopted 100% smoke-free campus policies.

sections.title: A wider range of community settings
paragraphs: The published record also describes support for Disneyland’s smoking and vaping ban. Its stated policy priorities include smoke-free city policies in Santa Ana, Stanton and Buena Park; voluntary smoke-free housing across Orange County; and eliminating sales and distribution of menthol and other flavored tobacco products in Fullerton and Stanton. These priorities should not be read as confirmation that every proposed measure was enacted.

sections.title: Take part
paragraphs: Residents, property representatives and community organizations can contact the team about educational materials, workgroups or technical support. For current legal requirements, consult the relevant city’s official rules.
